## What it is

`ffmpeg-skill` is an agent skill and MCP server designed for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. It bridges coding agents directly to local FFmpeg and Python standard libraries, giving them 42 structured tools to handle video processing tasks locally without uploading files or using cloud API keys.

## Why it matters

When AI agents try to edit video using raw shell strings, they often guess codecs, assume frame rates, and fail silently. This project replaces guesswork with a structured workflow: probe the input file first, edit using typed arguments, and verify the output using local checks and visual contact sheets.

## Key features

- Run 42 local video tools covering cuts, silence removal, captions, karaoke, and loudness normalisation
- Expose an MCP server with a machine-readable contract for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
- Verify every execution automatically using built-in probing, checks, and visual contact sheets
- Operate fully offline without cloud dependencies, subscriptions, or external API keys
- Generate runtime input schemas directly from the CLI argparse definitions to prevent contract drift

## Quick start

```bash
npx ffmpeg-skill
```

## Who should try it

This tool fits developers building local media pipelines, automated video generation workflows, or leveraging AI coding assistants for local file manipulation.

## Verdict

An essential utility for anyone building local AI media workflows, provided you already have FFmpeg and Python installed.

## What it is

ffmpeg-skill is an open-source Python project that bridges AI coding assistants directly to local video processing tools. It provides an agent skill and server implementation that exposes 42 typed tools for editing media without cloud dependencies.

## How it works

The project exposes local media utilities through a machine-readable contract. Instead of letting coding assistants guess command-line flags, it uses typed arguments and self-verification checks. Every editing job runs a mandatory probe phase to measure file properties before executing local operations.

## Key features

- Forty-two local video tools covering cuts, silence removal, captions, and loudness normalisation
- Model Context Protocol server integration for assistants like Claude Code and Cursor
- Automated verification using built-in probing and contact sheets
- Fully offline operation with no cloud dependencies or API keys
- Runtime input schemas generated from command-line argument definitions

## Getting started

Clone the repository from GitHub, ensure you have Python and FFmpeg installed locally, and configure the server inside your coding assistant environment.

## When not to use it

Skip this project if you do not use AI coding assistants or if your environment lacks a local installation of Python and FFmpeg.

# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native x86-64 application for Windows and Linux ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.1.0, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows and Linux; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.1.0, 1.2.1 and 1.4.3; 1.2.1 and 1.4.3 saves carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- HDR10 output with peak, game and HUD brightness settings
- 16:10 (Steam Deck, handhelds), 21:9 and 32:9

RustGIS

A fast, free and open-source GIS in pure Rust for mapping, analyzing and sharing geospatial data.
Native on Windows, macOS and Linux, and in your web browser. Your data stays on your machine unless you send it to an AI model you choose, and every action is a command you can script.

queue.readme_excerpt:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skil
